title: Towards a Unified Framework for Adaptable Problematic Content Detection via Continual Learning

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the classification models' ability to detect sexist, misogynistic, and targeted hateful content using few-shot and continual learning on datasets like Call Me Sexists But (CMSB), Misogyny Detection, Dygen (women/trans subsets), and HateCheck.

Measuring the models' performance in identifying hate speech and abusive text directed at specific racial and ethnic identities (e.g., Black, Asian, Indigenous, mixed race) using datasets such as Dygen, HateCheck, and Stormfront.

Assessing the few-shot and continual learning classification capabilities for detecting hate speech aimed at religious groups, primarily Muslims and Jews, using the Multitarget-CONAN, Dygen, and HateCheck datasets.
Evaluating the models' accuracy in identifying homophobia and hate speech targeting LGBTQ+ individuals and gender minorities using datasets like Multitarget-CONAN, Dygen, and HateCheck.

Testing the models on their ability to detect xenophobic hate speech and abuse directed against migrants, immigrants, asylum seekers, and refugees utilizing the Multitarget-CONAN, Dygen, and HateCheck datasets.
Measuring the classification performance on detecting hate speech and derogation targeting people with disabilities using targeted subsets from the Multitarget-CONAN and Dygen datasets.
